name: Amino Acid Biosynthesis Pathways
description: E. coli synthesizes all 20 amino acids from central metabolic intermediates (glycolysis, TCA cycle, pentose phosphate pathway). Major biosynthetic families include: glutamate family (Glu, Gln, Pro, Arg) from α-ketoglutarate; aspartate family (Asp, Asn, Met, Thr, Ile, Lys) from oxaloacetate; serine family (Ser, Gly, Cys) from 3-phosphoglycerate; aromatic family (Phe, Tyr, Trp) from PEP + E4P via shikimate; pyruvate family (Ala, Val, Leu) from pyruvate; and histidine from PRPP. Each pathway has 2-12 enzymatic steps with feedback inhibition by end products and transcriptional regulation by repressors (e.g., TrpR, ArgR). Branched pathways share common intermediates, creating metabolic networks with multiple choice points. This flowchart illustrates major amino acid families, branch points, regulatory mechanisms, and the integration of biosynthesis with central metabolism.
scientificAccuracy: Based on comprehensive biochemical and genetic characterization of E. coli amino acid biosynthesis. All pathways well-validated.
